title: standardize-ci-stage-annotations-and-constrain-dep-visibility
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Normalize CI stage annotations to power targeted dashboards and prune transient dev dependencies from release artifacts to reduce image size and accidental surface area. No runtime behavioral changes expected.
description:
Motivation: Our CI pipelines have grown ad-hoc stage names and use inconsistent annotations which makes observability and selective pipeline reruns brittle. Separately, the release build was accidentally packaging several transient dev/test dependencies (not needed for runtime or signing), increasing artifact size and expanding SBOM noise. This PR standardizes a compact set of CI stage annotations (stage:id, stage:kind, stage:provenance) that are applied consistently across composite/child workflows and the release signing job, and introduces a build-time 'dep-visibility' filter that excludes dev/test-only deps from the final release bundle.

What this changes (single continuous description): - Introduces a lightweight stage annotation schema and helper script (tools/ci/stage-annotate.py) used by composite actions and workflow templates so every job emits reproducible stage metadata. - Updates the workflow templates in .github/workflows/* to set annotation keys and make them queryable by the CI dashboard. - Adds dep-visibility control to build scripts (build/release_bundle.sh and tools/deps/filter_visibility.py) which prunes 'dev' and 'test' scope deps from the release artifact and SBOM. - Modifies the release-signing action inputs to accept explicit stage metadata so provenance is recorded alongside artifacts. - Adds unit tests for the filter and end-to-end smoke in the quickci lane to assert artifact size regression is within target.

Testing and validation: - Local unit tests: tools/deps/filter_visibility tests added. - CI: Quick-feedback lane run (test/quickci) and nightly release-smoke both exercised the change. There was an intermittent lint job failure on the first run (flake in golangci-lint config) which was fixed by a small lint config tweak (see commit 3). - Integration: produced a signed release candidate in the staging bucket and verified SBOM no longer contains dev-only packages and artifact size reduced by ~3.8MB.

Rollout plan: - Deploy new workflow templates to main (this PR). - Monitor nightly release-smoke and the CI dashboard for stage annotation ingestion. - If any compatibility issue appears with external partners who parse release metadata, fall back to the previous signing job for a single release while we migrate partners.

Checklist: - [x] Stage annotation schema and helper implemented - [x] Workflow templates updated - [x] Dep visibility filter implemented and unit-tested - [x] Release signing inputs updated and smoke-tested - [x] Documentation note added to docs/dev/ci.md and docs/releasenotes/visibility.md

References: Linear ENG-1729 (ci stage observability), ENG-1731 (release artifact hygiene).

review_comments: Liam O'Connor (2026-03-01): Nice consolidation. Two asks: (1) can the annotation helper be a tiny Go binary to avoid Python in some runners? (2) please add a quick dashboard query example in docs so SRE can onboard the dashboard.

Maya Patel (2026-03-01): Reply to Liam: We chose Python to keep the helper portable across hosted runners without extra build step; it is intentionally minimal. I added a doc snippet with the PromQL query and a note about conversion if we later rewrite to Go.
Priya Ramesh (2026-03-02): Requested change: The filter should log removed deps to a stable path for auditing; please include the log file so we can compare pre/post SBOMs.
Maya Patel (2026-03-02): Addressed: filter_visibility now writes removed_deps.log and quickci validates presence and non-empty content. Added test asserting entries are present when filtered.
Ethan Zhao (2026-03-02): Approve after small nit on the release.yml comment formatting.
notes_on_ci: CI initially reported a failing lint shard (golangci flake) on the first run; a follow-up commit adjusted .golangci.yml and re-ran the matrix. Quickci lane passed on rerun; nightly release-smoke passed and produced the signed candidate. Full pipeline artifacts uploaded to staging for verification.
test_matrix_summary: quickci (fast unit + smoke) — pass; integration/nightly release-smoke — pass; full integration matrix (runtime/serving) — unchanged and green in downstream job; lint matrix flake fixed and rerun passed.
risk_assessment: Low. Changes are build-time only and guarded by unit tests and quickci smoke. Risk vector is limited to release metadata consumers; we added a compatibility note and fallback plan in docs. Monitoring: artifact size and SBOM drift monitored for three releases post-merge.
notes: This PR is intentionally focused on hygiene and observability; it does not touch runtime serving code or change model artifacts. If any partner integration fails to consume new stage metadata, we will fallback to a signing job that mirrors old metadata for a single release while we coordinate the migration.
